observation.visible_scene: A still landscape of a calm mountain lake under a clear blue sky. A snow-capped jagged mountain ridge spans the background; a golden-brown grassy hillside with bare shrubs and a small tree on its crest slopes down from the left to the water's edge. The lower half of the frame is the lake surface, which mirrors the mountains, hillside and sky. A few thin bare branches enter from the right edge and bottom-left corner, and a small light-colored structure is visible (and reflected) on the far right shore.
visible_changes: The actual terrain elements — the snow-capped peaks, the left hillside, the sky, the right-side branches and the distant structure — hold fixed pixel positions across all frames, indicating no camera pan, tilt or zoom.

The only visible motion is in the water: gentle surface ripples continuously deform the mirror reflection, causing the reflected white mountain band and the reflected golden slope to wobble, stretch and shift slightly up and down between frames (e.g. the reflection pattern differs frame-to-frame while the real mountains above stay identical).
The ripple texture across the open water in the foreground changes subtly from frame to frame, an ongoing process already present at t=0 and still present at the last frame.
The reflected image remains a reflection of the same scene (it tracks the static mountains/hill), not a separate moving object.
outside_clip_unknowns: The cause of the ripples (wind, a distant disturbance, etc.) is not shown.
Whether the ripple motion persists, grows or settles after the crop boundary is unknown.
uncertain_details: The exact amplitude and wavelength of the surface ripples are small and hard to quantify frame-by-frame.
Any sub-pixel camera drift cannot be fully excluded, but background landmarks appear stationary, so the camera is effectively fixed.
